source.citation: Arabic Language Learning Notes (アラビア語学習メモ), Learn How to Write Arabic Letters — Basic Naskh: Taa Marbuta ة, isolated form and stroke order (updated 2022-03-31; accessed 2026-08-23)
source.variation: The lesson identifies ة as a word-final-only form with isolated ة and connected final ـة shapes. For the isolated form it explicitly starts at the body's upper point, circles clockwise through a compact triangular o-shape resting on the baseline, and adds the two upper dots afterward. It notes that instructional traditions differ on whether the right or left dot comes first; this learner path follows the left-then-right order already used by the source-backed Arabic ت record. The Open University's introductory Arabic course independently confirms that ة occurs only word-finally, distinguishes its isolated and connected-final shapes, and explains its pause h versus linked t behavior. The path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline without treating this ending as a base letter.
